title: Effects of Light Crystal Display 3D-Printing Technology, Storage Time and Steam Sterilization on Dimensional Stability of a Photopolymer Resin for Surgical Guides: An In-Vitro Study
content:
Background: Implant surgical guides manufactured in-house using 3D- printing technology are widely used in clinical practice to transfer virtual planning to the operative field. 
Aim: The present in-vitro study investigated the dimensional changes of 3D-surgical guides printed in-house using the Shining 3D surgical guide resin (SG01).
Materials and methods: Five test bodies, different in shapes and dimensions, were designed using a computer-aided design (CAD) software program and manufactured by the three Light Crystal Display (LCD) 3D- printers. Specific printing and post-processing parameters of SG01 resin were set to manufacture 25 test bodies from each printer. Dimensional changes of 75 samples were evaluated using a digital calliper at four different time points: immediately after printing (T0), one month after storage (T1), immediately after sterilization (T2), and one month after sterilization (T3).
Results: All test bodies showed deviations from the overall CAD reference value of 12.25 mm after printing and post-processing (T0) and following steam sterilization (T2). Similar trends were observed for the effect of storage times at T1 and T3. The AccuFab prints demonstrated better dimensional stability than the Elegoo and Zortrax samples.
Conclusions: LCD-3D printers, sterilization, and storage times influenced the dimensional stability of test bodies made with SGO1 resin.
